Random-effects meta-analysis (blocker.stan): one row per trial (22 trials), treatment (nt,rt) and control (nc,rc) arms in the same row (wide); the study-level random effect delta[N] is observation-level (one row per study), no grouping column in the table.

Latent-trait/item-response model (bones.stan): the loaded table holds item parameters (ncat, delta, gamma_1..4) for 34 indicators, not observations; the response (grade, child-by-indicator matrix) and the grouping (child, theta[nChild]) are not columns.
Avoidance-learning model (dogs.stan): wide table, 30 dogs as rows and 25 trials as Y_1..Y_25 columns; only fixed effects (alpha, beta), no random effect; grouping unit (dog) is no long column.

One-way variance-components model (dyes.stan): wide table, 6 batches as rows and 5 samples as y_1..y_5 columns; the batch random effect is a row and samples are columns, so the grouping factor is no column of the loaded table.

Hierarchical Poisson (epil.stan): wide table, 59 patients as rows and 4 visits as y_1..y_4 columns; per-patient random effects index rows (observation-level) and visit is columns; grouping unit is no long column.
Bioequivalence cross-over (equiv.stan): wide table, 10 subjects as rows and 2 periods as Y_1,Y_2 columns; the subject random effect delta[N] indexes rows (observation-level) and period is columns.

Weibull frailty survival (kidney.stan). RULE GAP: the loader tabulated only the length-18 right-censored arrays (age_rc, sex_rc, patient_rc, t_rc, disease_rc); the 58 uncensored observations and their event times are separate arrays flagged not-in-table, so the loaded table is a censored-only subset (t_rc holds censoring times, patient_rc has 15 of 38 patients, mostly singletons). Excluded as a partial/derived slice; re-file if the full long table is wanted.

Cox regression (leuk.stan): single fixed covariate Z (treatment) and baseline hazard dL0; no random effect and no grouping column (one row per patient). The frailty version leukfr adds the pair random effect and is kept.

Rasch item-response model (lsat.stan): wide/aggregated table of 32 response patterns (response_1..5 items as columns, culm = cumulative pattern counts); the student random effect theta[N] indexes 1000 students not in the table.

Random-effects meta-analysis (magnesium.stan): one row per study (8 studies), treatment (nt,rt) and control (nc,rc) arms in the same row (wide); the study-level random effect theta is observation-level, no grouping column.

Weibull regression (mice.stan): beta[group] is a fixed effect per dose group (M=4, flat normal(0,100) prior, no hyperparameter), not a random effect; only 4 groups; loaded table is the uncensored subset (group_uncensored, t_uncensored). Fixed-effects fit, no hierarchical model.

Case-control smoothing of log-odds (oxford.stan): wide table, one row per year-stratum (120 strata), case arm (r1,n1) and control arm (r0,n0) in the same row; the per-stratum random effect b[K] is observation-level.
Gamma-Poisson failure model (pump.stan): 10 pumps as 10 rows (count x, exposure t); theta[N] is a per-pump gamma random effect, observation-level (one Poisson row per pump), no grouping column.
Poisson GLMM with overdispersion (salm.stan): wide table, 6 doses as rows and 3 plates as y_1..y_3 columns; the dose random effect lambda indexes rows (observation-level) and plates are columns.
Same as salm (salm2.stan, uncentred covariates): wide table of 6 doses x 3 plates (y_1..y_3); the dose random effect is observation-level and plates are columns.

Read help labels and first rows. Wide multi-span format: time1-time17 and numkid1-numkid17 are the fertility spans as columns, one row per respondent (#23 wide-table rule); the long per-span versions are divorce/divorce2.
Read help labels (w1sesl_m = 'aggregated mean ses from child level'). One row per school, aggregated up from ecls_child; a derived summary of another object of this source.

Read help (no labels) and first rows. Meta-analysis of 19 teacher-expectancy studies, one row per study (est, se); the study-level effect is an observation-level random effect, no within-study replication.
Read ch1.do: only regress (OLS) fits, no random term; faculty salary data, one row per faculty member with no cluster column.
Read help (no labels) and first rows. Age-at-first-intercourse survival in person format, one row per subject (id unique); no repeated person-period cluster in the loaded table.
Read help labels and first rows. Wooldridge cross-sectional worker fringe-benefits data, one row per worker; industry appears only as a handful of ind1-ind9 dummies (covariates), no sampled cluster.
Read help labels and first rows. Wide repeated-measures: gpa1-gpa6 and job1-job6 are six semesters as columns, one row per student (#23 wide-table rule).
Read help and first rows. Wide two-grader reliability subset of essays: grade1 and grade4 are two graders as columns, one row per essay (#23 wide-table rule).
Read help and first rows. Frets' head-dimensions data, length1/breadth1/length2/breadth2 are first- and second-son measurements as columns, one row per family (#23 wide-table rule).

ch13 fits a Poisson disease-mapping model (gllamm o, i(county) offset(lne)) but the table has 56 rows, one per Scottish county (o observed, e expected cases): county is an observation-level random effect, not a grouping factor (melanoma/#24 convention).
Wide repeated-measures: one row per subject (subj), depression scores dep1-dep6 the six occasions in columns; the grouping unit (occasion) is no column of the table (#23 wide rule).

ch14 expands this one-row-per-academic table (id unique, 301 rows) into person-year records for a discrete-time survival logit; the loaded table itself is single-spell (dur, event) with no clustering column.

ch7 fits mixed read grade || id: grade after reshaping to long, but the loaded table is wide: one row per student (id), read0-read3/math0-math3/age0-age3 the four occasions in columns (#23 wide rule).
Single-spell recidivism duration (durat, cens), one row per released inmate (1445 rows); no clustering column to index random effects.
Wide repeated-measures: one row per patient (id), score1-score4 the four post-op occasions in columns; the grouping unit is no column (#23 wide rule).

Wide repeated-measures: one row per patient, respiratory status v1-v4 the four visits in columns (bl the baseline); the occasion grouping is no column (#23 wide rule). center clusters patients but the repeated response is spread across columns.
Map boundary coordinates (lon, lat) of 1515 polygon vertices for the Scottish lip-cancer regions (regcode/regid); a geographic layout, not grouped observations (coordinate rule, #22/#23).
56-row region-level summary of the lips lip-cancer analysis: observed cases with crude and model-predicted SMRs (smr_normal, smr_npml are fitted values). A derived results table, one row per region.
Single-spell survival of teacher tenure (t, censor), one row per teacher (id unique, 3941 rows); no clustering column.
ch12 fits mlogit alt Hinc Psize: one row per traveler (210 rows), alt the chosen mode; a cross-sectional multinomial with no repeated grouping (the long version is travel2).
Wide/aggregated twin data: twin1 and twin2 hold the two members' values in columns with a frequency count (num2) and zygosity (dzmz); no long grouping column for the pair.
ch10 fits logit workstat husbinc i.chilpres (Fox women's labour-force data): one row per wife (263 rows), a single cross-section with no clustering column; region is a fixed locality.
ROS Peacekeeping example (peace.R): survival / censored time-to-ceasefire-failure, one row per conflict episode (country-conflict); delay is the time, censored? the indicator. No repeated cluster.

ROS PearsonLee example: frequency-weighted table of child vs parent heights (regress child ~ parent). frequency is a weight; gp/par/chl are parent-child sex labels (4 combinations), no sampling cluster.
ROS Pollution example: 60 SMSA cities, one row per city (McDonald-Schwing mortality regression) mort ~ pollution + demographics; no grouping factor.
Stata twin of Pollution/data/pollution.csv; 60 cities, one row per city, no grouping factor.
ROS Poststrat example: 778 respondents (vote and pid = party, 3 levels, the predictor); one row per respondent, no sampling cluster.
ROS RiskyBehavior example (risky.R): Poisson/neg-bin glm of fupacts (follow-up unprotected acts) on treatment (couples/women_alone); one row per subject, no repeated cluster.
ROS Roaches example (roaches.R): Poisson glm of y (roach count) ~ roach1 + treatment + senior with offset exposure2; one row per apartment, no grouping factor.
ROS SIS data: 1501 persons, income/benefit components; one row per person, no grouping factor.
Raw Stata source (28 cols) of Sesame/data/sesame.csv (filed in the registry); same 240 children, duplicate of the Sesame study.
ROS Student (UCI math course): one row per student; school is a 2-level fixed predictor (GP/MS) used among 26 covariates in stan_glm(G3mat ~ .), not a sampling cluster.
ROS Student merged-all (682 rows): one row per student, school a 2-level fixed predictor, no grouping factor.
ROS Student merged math+Portuguese (students common to both): one row per student, 2-level school predictor, no grouping factor.
ROS Student (UCI Portuguese course): one row per student, school a 2-level fixed predictor, no sampling cluster; stan_glm(G3por ~ .) classical.
ROS Names example: wide table, 98012 names x 134 year-count columns (X1880..X2010); a name-by-year count matrix, no grouping factor (wide format).

ROS Beauty example (beauty.R): classical stan_glm(eval ~ beauty + female), one row per course evaluation. course_id is unusable as a cluster: 306 of 463 rows carry the catch-all 0, lumping many single-taught courses into one pseudo-group.
ROS Bypass example: 200 patients, one row each (age, severity, new, stay); no grouping factor.
ROS ChileSchools example (chile_schools.R): regression-discontinuity stan_glm(read92 ~ eligible + rule2); one row per school, cmb_regn a 4-level combined region (covariate), no repeated cluster.
ROS Congress example: wide table, one row per congressional district with 3 election years (inc86/88/90, v86/88/90); wide repeated-measures layout, no grouping column.
ROS Coins/HeadsSchools example: 11-row frequency table (x = number of heads, count); a histogram, no grouping factor.
ROS ElectionsEconomy (Hibbs bread-and-peace): 16 elections, vote ~ growth; one point per election year, a time series with no replication.
ROS Incentives example: 62 rows (rr_diff, value, prepay, gift, burden); meta-analysis of survey-incentive conditions with no study/survey id column in the table, no grouping factor.
ROS KidIQ example: classical lm(kid_score ~ mom_hs + mom_iq + ...); one row per child, no grouping factor (same data as stan_arm kidiq).
ROS LowBwt example: Hosmer-Lemeshow low-birth-weight data, one row per infant (ID row id); glm(low ~ ...), no grouping factor.
ROS Mesquite example: lm(weight ~ diam + height + density + group); group a 2-level site/batch covariate, 46 bushes one row each, no clustering unit (as stan_arm mesquite).
ROS Mile example: world-record mile times by year, 32-row time series, no replication.
ROS Gay example: 81422 respondents x 7 columns (age, gender, race, gay-marriage attitudes); no state or cluster column in this extract, one row per respondent.

ROS AcademyAwards data (oscars.csv/txt): no model script in the repo and no documented response. Comp (318 competition/choice sets) repeats and would support a conditional-logit Oscar-winner model, but no column is a clean per-competition winner (PrW takes 0/1/2/3 and sums to 0 for most Comps), so there is no defensible response. RULE GAP: a repeating choice-set grouping with no identifiable response; excluded rather than guess a winner column.
ROS Poststrat poll (rda twin of Poststrat/data/poll.csv): 778 respondents, vote and pid only, no sampling cluster.
ROS Pollution (rda twin of pollution.csv): 60 cities one row each, no grouping factor.
ROS RiskyBehavior (rda twin of risky.csv): one row per subject, Poisson count outcome, no grouping factor.
ROS Coop example: 27 rows, candidate names with vote tallies at 6 time points (V2-V7); a wide election-count time series, no grouping column.
ROS Roaches (rda twin of roaches.csv): one row per apartment, Poisson count, no grouping factor.
ROS SexRatio example: 5-row aggregate (x attractiveness, y percent girls); no grouping, no replication.
ROS Student (rda twin of student-merged.csv): one row per student; school is a 2-level fixed predictor used among 26 covariates (stan_glm(G3mat ~ .)), not a sampling cluster.
ROS Arsenic/Wells example: glm(switched ~ dist + arsenic + educ, binomial); one row per household, no grouping factor (as stan_arm wells).
7-column model extract of the NYC HVS rodent data (y, race, floor, dist, bldg); same 15894 apartments as Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed), derived.
1748-row subset of apt.dat / the HVS rodent data, derived.
54-column all-variables version of the HVS rodent apartment data (15894 rows); duplicate of Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed).
459-row subset of the HVS rodent data, derived.
20-column unsorted version of Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed), same 15894 rows, duplicate.
1748-row subset of the HVS rodent data (51 columns incl. rodent2 and group means); subset of the study filed as hvs02_sorted.csv.

Wide repeated-measures: one row per subject (only 5 subjects) with 16 estrone-assay 'vial' columns; the within-subject replicate is no column of the loaded table. estrlong.sav is the long twin kept in the registry.
Twelve rows of two test scores (ALGEBRA, STATS), a correlation/reliability example with no id or grouping column; wide, no grouping unit in the table.

Meta-analysis effect-size table: 20 rows, one effect size (d) per study, 'study' never repeats, so no grouping factor has within-group replication (contrast MetaResp/MultResp, where study repeats over modes). An aggregate of study summaries.

Wide form of the AstLrd asthma/LRD meta-analysis: one row per study with asthma and LRD odds ratios spread across columns (many NaN); the study-level grouping collapses to one row each. AstLrd.sav is the long twin.

Wide round-robin sociometric table: one row per child with 11 RATING columns (ratings received from groupmates); the sender/receiver dyadic grouping is spread across columns. SocsLong.sav is the long twin kept in the registry.
Snijders & Bosker Table 3.1 (artificial clustered-data illustration): 10 rows with 10 group columns Y1-Y10; the groups are columns, not a grouping factor in the table (wide).

The same partnership event-history file as goldstein_partnership/partnership.txt, read here without a header row (the first data row became the column names: '1.0000','16.',...). The named copy under goldstein_partnership is kept in the registry.

A multiple-membership reshape of the Project STAR data (star1.dta, in the registry): teacher membership is spread over some 80 wide weight columns, which the registry cannot represent; the first reader had filed a plain school intercept and flagged it, the blind reader excluded it (verdict 2026-10-08).

One row per respondent of the ROS earnings example; ethnicity (four levels) is a demographic covariate, not a sampled cluster (the #23 area-factor rule), and the ARM varying-intercept model on it does not make it one; the first reader had flagged the row, the blind reader excluded it (verdict 2026-10-08).

A single-level conditional logit (ch 12): traveler is the choice-set identifier, not a sampled cluster, so the chapter model carries no random term (Alex, spot check 2026-10-08; a departure from the #23 rendering of conditional-logistic designs with a random intercept on the set).

ROS fits partyid7 ~ real_ideo + race_adj + factor(age_discrete) + educ1 + female + income separately within each year: the survey wave is modelled as fixed and is no grouping factor (#23 rule; Alex, spot check 2026-10-08).
The rpackage rendering of the NES file: ROS fits the party-identification regression separately within each year, the wave modelled as fixed (#23 rule; Alex, spot check 2026-10-08).

The storable-votes ordered logit (ch 15) fits vote ~ value to individual participants one at a time; neither person nor the two-level school is a random grouping factor in the documented model (Alex, spot check 2026-10-08).
As 2playergames.csv: the ordered logit is fitted per participant, no random grouping (Alex, spot check 2026-10-08).
As 2playergames.csv: the ordered logit is fitted per participant, no random grouping (Alex, spot check 2026-10-08).

A full-factorial greenhouse experiment on Triadica, one row per experimental unit; replicate is the design index of the factorial, not a repeated observational cluster (blind reading, confirmed by Alex 2026-10-08).
